key_themes: AI hardware budget shift crushes IBM, dragging software/consulting sector
China memory chip competition sparks Micron selloff, pulls AMD, Intel, Marvell lower
PayPal M&A surge on $53B Stripe/Advent takeover report; Apple AI approval in China hits record high

stocks.reason: Stock crashed ~25% Tuesday (worst day since 1968) after Q2 revenue warning: $17.2B vs $17.86B estimate; CEO cited clients shifting capex from IBM software to AI hardware/chips. Recovering slightly Wednesday; Oppenheimer downgraded.
Surged ~17% on report that Stripe and Advent International made a $60.50/share (~$53B) takeover bid, nearly 28% above prior close; trading volume 446% above average.
Gained ~4% to notch a new all-time high after report that Apple received Chinese regulatory approval to launch generative AI features in China, a key growth market.
Rose 7%+ on Q2 earnings beat — AUM, ETF inflows, and fee income topped expectations. On pace for best single day in over a year.
Fell ~8% after a report on Chinese memory chipmakers raised fears of intensifying competition, dragging the broader semiconductor group lower.
Q2 earnings beat with €9.3B net sales and €2.9B net income; raised full-year 2026 sales outlook to €43-45B and gross margin guidance to 54-56% (from 51-53%). Shares jumped in premarket.
Surged ~9.4% after Benzinga analysts forecast a 12%+ rally; bullish momentum driven by cybersecurity demand and positive analyst attention on Wednesday.
Dropped 5%+ in sympathy with Micron on China memory competition fears, part of a broad semiconductor sector selloff hitting memory and chip names.
Fell below $135 IPO price for the first time, down ~34% from post-IPO highs; fourth consecutive down session after joining Nasdaq-100 last week.
Tumbled ~7% despite reporting Q2 revenue above consensus and raising full-year EPS guidance; market interpreted results negatively on margin pressures.
On pace for worst week of 2026, down 5%+ this week after a cyclospora outbreak linked to KFC and Taco Bell locations rattled investors and raised food-safety liability concerns.
Reported Q2 2026 earnings with revenue per available seat mile up 12.1% YoY; guided for even stronger growth in H2 2026 on strong international demand.
Reported Q2 earnings highlighted by wealth management inflows and investment banking fee recovery; shares moved on results as part of the ongoing bank earnings cycle.
Sold off in sympathy with IBM as investors worried that AI hardware budget shifts will reduce enterprise software spending across the sector; Workday and Adobe also affected.
